chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from some of his companions raising it (to the Prophet), said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) used to dislike black, except in three (garments): the leather sock, the turban, and the cloak.

key_terms.السَّوَاد: Black; blackness; the color black in garments
key_terms.الْخُفّ: Khuff — leather footwear (sock/slipper) worn over bare feet, relevant in ablution discussions
key_terms.الْعِمَامَة: 'Imama — turban, a traditional head covering of religious and social significance
key_terms.الْكِسَاء: Kisa' — a loose outer cloak or mantle; also the garment of the hadith of al-Kisa'
key_terms.رَفَعَهُ: Rafa'ahu — he raised it; a technical term indicating the chain is elevated directly to the Prophet
key_terms.يَكْرَه: Yakrahu — he dislikes; in jurisprudence, 'makruh' denotes a discouraged but not forbidden act

ai.seo_question: Did the Prophet Muhammad dislike wearing black clothing?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) had a personal aversion to wearing black, with three specific exceptions: the khuff (leather sock worn over the foot), the imama (turban), and the kisa' (outer cloak or mantle). In early Islamic jurisprudence, this prophetic preference (makruh/disliked) shaped Shia scholarly discussions on the permissibility of black clothing, particularly in formal and ritual contexts. The hadith is transmitted via a mursal (elevated) chain through Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi.
